top_stories.ai_overview: Artificial Intelligence Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS Today, we are announcing the availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic’s most capable generally available model for technical work that raises the bar in coding and the sciences.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs for advanced work in cyber security and life sciences.
ai_key_details: In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock.
Why Claude Fable 5.2 Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science.

In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1.
Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes.

ai_key_takeaways: It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days.
If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5.
On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch.

top_stories.ai_overview: In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99%.
top_stories.ai_what_happened: Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers.
ai_key_details: They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts.
These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost.
Zhipu, for example, distilled the cyber capabilities of leading US models during the development of GLM-5.3.
The US Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) has since assessed GLM-5.3 to be the most cyber-capable open-weights model released to date.
top_stories.ai_why_it_matters: First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards.
